name: MARAFON
description: Marafon (also known as Beccaccino) is the 'King of Romagna Card Games', a sophisticated partnership trick-taking game played with a 40-card Italian deck. It combines the precise point-structure of Tressette (where 3s and 2s are high) with the power of a Trump suit. Famous for its 'silent play' etiquette and complex signaling system, it demands perfect memory and seamless teamwork. A match typically races to 41 points, with bonuses for holding the 'Cricca' (the top three trumps).

content.text: Marafon (also known as Beccaccino) is the 'King of Romagna Card Games', a sophisticated partnership trick-taking game played with a 40-card Italian deck. It combines the precise point-structure of Tressette (where 3s and 2s are high) with the power of a Trump suit. Famous for its 'silent play' etiquette and complex signaling system, it demands perfect memory and seamless teamwork. A match typically races to 41 points, with bonuses for holding the 'Cricca' (the top three trumps).
Developed in the 19th century in the Romagna region (ForlÃ¬, Ravenna, Cesena) as an evolution of Tressette, adding the concept of 'Trionfo' (Trump) to the rigorous ranking system.
4 players in two fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite).
40 cards. Ranking in all suits: 3 (Highest), 2, Ace, King, Knight (Cavallo), Jack (Fante), 7, 6, 5, 4 (Lowest).
Italian deck (or 52-card deck with 8s, 9s, 10s removed). Score sheet.
Dealer deals 10 cards to each player. The Trump suit is determined by turning the last card dealt to the dealer (or by dealer declaration in some variants).

items.text: Beccaccino Proper: Usually played to 31 points instead of 41. Often allows 'Busso' only.
Tressette a Donne: Variant where declarations (Napola) are more elaborate, including sets of 3s, 2s, or Aces.
